reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly shows that a 10.2 at.% Al coating had the best corrosion resistance and a denser Nb2Zr6O17/ZrO2 oxide layer, supporting the key premises. However, the evidence is from a single study under PWR conditions, not high-temperature steam LOCA conditions, so the extrapolation to 800 °C steam is a minor gap.
premises: AlNbTiZr MEA coatings with ~10 at.% Al form a dense oxide layer of Nb2Zr6O17 and ZrO2
This dense oxide layer improves corrosion/oxidation resistance and reduces oxygen penetration
There is an optimum Al content (~10 at.%) for best performance, with lower or higher Al being worse
The coating can be applied to zirconium-alloy cladding and tested under high-temperature steam conditions
